message.reasoning:
Given this is a huge class, I'm planning a JUnit 4 test suite focused on a manageable but comprehensive set of methods -- covering emptiness checks, trimming, and stripping variants with their key branches.

Given the sheer scope of StringUtils methods, I'll write a comprehensive test class covering most of them grouped logically, accepting I can't exhaustively test every single method given effort constraints. I also need to watch for internal dependencies on ArrayUtils, CharUtils, SystemUtils, ObjectUtils, and CharSequenceUtils as I write these tests.

Writing test methods...

Continuing through more test cases: stripAll variants, equals/equalsIgnoreCase comparisons, and various indexOf and ordinalIndexOf lookups covering null, empty, and positional matching scenarios.

26-37. Continuing the test case list through lastIndexOf variants (char, String, with/without startPos), lastIndexOfIgnoreCase edge cases, contains/containsIgnoreCase checks, and indexOfAny/containsAny lookups against character and string arrays.

38-47. I continue mapping out tests for containsAny with null search arrays, indexOfAnyBut/containsOnly/containsNone against char arrays and strings (covering null/empty edge cases plus true/false normal cases), indexOfAny/lastIndexOfAny with String arrays including null entries, and substring edge cases with negative or out-of-range start positions.

48-58. I keep listing substring/left/right/mid variants with their null, negative, and boundary edge cases, then move to substringBefore/After/BeforeLast/AfterLast tests checking null and empty separators plus found/not-found scenarios, finishing with substringBetween and substringsBetween tests covering missing delimiters and null/empty open tags.

I continue through split variants (by char, string, with max count, whole separator, preserve-all-tokens versions), character-type splitting, then move into the join family covering object arrays, iterators, and different separator/range combinations.

After that I work through whitespace deletion, start/end removal (with case-insensitive variants), text replacement functions (single, multiple, repeated, character-based), overlay, chomp, chop, repeat, and padding utilities like rightPad.

I continue cataloging case transformation methods (upperCase, lowerCase with locale support, capitalize, swapCase), character-matching checks (isAlpha, isNumeric, isWhitespace variants), and finally defaultString helpers for null-safe string handling.

Still listing more methods... difference checks, Levenshtein distance, startsWith/endsWith variants. Given the scope, I accept this will require a fairly long, comprehensive test class covering most of these branches, keeping individual test methods concise but numerous.
